import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Chvátal's Conjecture

*References:*

* [A Conjecture in Extremal Combinatorics](https://users.encs.concordia.ca/~chvatal/conjecture.html)
* [Chvátal's Conjecture and Correlation Inequalities](https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.08954)
-/

namespace Chvatal

variable {α : Type} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]

/-- A family F of sets is Decreasing if it is closed under taking subsets. -/
def Decreasing (F : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
    ∀ A B : Finset α, B ⊆ A → A ∈ F → B ∈ F

/-- A family F of sets is Intersecting if each pair of members has nonempty intersection. -/
def Intersecting (F : Finset (Finset α)) : Prop :=
    ∀ A ∈ F, ∀ B ∈ F, A ∩ B ≠ ∅

/--
If F is a decreasing family of sets of some finite type α, then there is some element
x of α such that the family consisting of all members of F containing x is an intersecting
subfamily of F with maximal cardinality.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem exists_maximal_star :
    ∀ F : Finset (Finset α), Decreasing F →
        ∃ x : α, ∀ G, G ⊆ F → Intersecting G → G.card ≤ { A ∈ F | x ∈ A }.card := by
  sorry

reformulations.difference: Chvátal's web page treats {∅} as intersecting and excludes F = {∅}. Lean instead requires intersections for all pairs, including equal members, and includes F = {∅}. It also expresses 'largest intersecting subfamily' through a universal cardinality bound without explicitly asserting that the star is an intersecting subfamily.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The cited paper's definition of intersecting agrees exactly with Lean. Compared with the web-page convention, the only additional intersecting family is {∅}. If F ≠ {∅} contains this family, F has a nonempty member A. Applying Lean's bound to the intersecting singleton family {A} forces the selected star to have cardinality at least 1, so it also dominates {∅}. For F = {∅}, Lean's only intersecting subfamily is the empty family, making the added case true. The reverse implication follows by restricting the web-page bound to Lean-intersecting families. Finally, the filtered star is automatically a subfamily of F, and any two members intersect at its center x; hence the universal bound states precisely that it is largest. These equivalences were proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as Review.starProperty_iff_pageProperty, Review.conjecture_iff_page_conjecture, and Review.largest_star_iff.

sources_consulted: https://users.encs.concordia.ca/~chvatal/conjecture.html — definitions, the singleton-empty exception, and the conjecture.
https://arxiv.org/abs/1608.08954 — Friedgut, Kahn, Kalai and Keller, Chvátal's Conjecture and Correlation Inequalities.
https://arxiv.org/e-print/1608.08954 — LaTeX source; introductory definitions, Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 2.1, and the discussion of variants and average-case results.
https://dwest.web.illinois.edu/regs/chvatal.html — Variations on Chvátal's Conjecture (2009), linked from Chvátal's page.
review.notes: Checked both definitions and the theorem. The statement matches Conjecture 1.1 of the cited paper. Exhaustive Lean computations verified all decreasing families on ground sets of sizes 1, 2, and 3; separate checks covered the empty family, {∅}, and the necessity of a nonempty ground type. A nondecreasing triangle family fails the conclusion, confirming that the decreasing hypothesis is substantive. No status discrepancy was found in the accessible cited sources; the paper's proved average-case variants do not settle the general conjecture. A supplementary attempt to consult erdosproblems.com/701 was blocked by a browser challenge.
